title: Switzerland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Bodensee-Arena Leistungsofferte HLKS inkl. Gebäudeautomation und Fachkoordination
description: La Bodensee-Arena est un complexe sportif, de loisirs et d'événements majeur de la région de Kreuzlingen-Constance. Créé en 1978 et agrandi à plusieurs reprises, ce complexe présente un besoin important de rénovation sur les plans architectural, technique et opérationnel. La ville de Kreuzlingen prévoit la rénovation du complexe existant et la transformation de l'actuelle patinoire extérieure en salle d'entraînement. La structure existante doit être réutilisée dans la mesure où cela s’avère techniquement et économiquement justifié. La réalisation se fera par étapes, en tenant compte de l’exploitation en cours. Le crédit d’investissement de 26,7 millions de francs suisses a été approuvé lors du référendum du 28 septembre 2025. Ce montant constitue le plafond financier contraignant de l’ensemble du projet. La conception doit être développée de manière cohérente selon le principe du « Design-to-Cost ». Dans le cadre d’une procédure d’appel d’offres sélective avec préqualification (phase 1) suivie d’une soumission d’offres (phase 2), un bureau d’études qualifié en CVC est recherché pour la conception CVC, y compris l’automatisation du bâtiment (MSRL) et la coordination technique. Le bureau doit couvrir l’ensemble des domaines techniques faisant l’objet de l’appel d’offres et assumer la responsabilité globale de la coordination et de l’intégration des prestations dans le cadre du mandat. Le mandat comprend les prestations prévues par la norme SIA 108 pour les phases 31 à 53, de la conception à la mise en service. Les différents niveaux de modernisation des installations techniques existantes, l'intégration de la récupération de la chaleur résiduelle provenant du système de refroidissement de la patinoire, ainsi que la coordination de l'approvisionnement en énergie et des installations techniques dans le bâtiment principal existant et dans la nouvelle salle d'entraînement constituent des défis particuliers. Il s’agit de trouver des solutions économiques et efficaces sur le plan énergétique, qui tiennent compte des différentes utilisations et conditions d’exploitation et permettent une réalisation par étapes tout en préservant autant que possible le fonctionnement courant. Les interfaces avec les études de réfrigération et d’électricité, faisant l’objet de marchés distincts, doivent être assurées.

Les interfaces avec les systèmes CVC et d’automatisation du bâtiment, pour lesquels des marchés distincts ont été passés, avec la conception du système de refroidissement de la patinoire ainsi qu’avec la protection contre l’incendie doivent être coordonnées et validées dès le début du projet. Nous recherchons des solutions économiques, efficaces sur le plan énergétique et fiables, qui répondent aux exigences de l’ensemble du projet et respectent le plafond budgétaire imposé.

title: V301--539 - Fifth Floor Pharmacy Move Service Contract
description: The Cincinnati Veterans Administration Medical Center (VAMC) has a requirement to move the inpatient pharmacy to either to the second floor or the eight floor (back up eighth floor depending on room availability). The intention of this Sources Sought is to obtain information only. Please do not send a proposal. Requested information: To aid acquisition planning, we re seeking capable and interested firms for the information requested. If your firm meets the criteria please send the point of contract (ronald.heidemann@va.gov) the following, via email: Firm s Name Socio-Economic Status Whether or not your company has a contract vehicle we can order against If your company believes there is an alternative NAICS code please provide this If your company has any questions please provide. PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 1.0 BACKGROUND The Cincinnati VA Medical Center (VAMC) will be activating a new air handler unit for pharmacy with the potential move date being late-2026/early-2027, November-May. Due to personnel constraints, we are requesting the use of specialized movers to relocate medical equipment and testing needed to keep up with current inpatient care medication. The current pharmaceutical iv hoods, 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, OH 45220 fifth floor will be required to move to second floor (back up eighth floor depending on room availability). This will allow room certification testing so the Cincinnati pharmacy department can continue to create medications for patients within the hospital and CLC. SCOPE OF WORK The purpose of this contract is to provide relocation and moving services for the VA Medical Center at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, OH 45220. Moving and relocation services could include disassembly and assembly of iv hoods, disconnecting and reconnecting of medical equipment, disconnecting and reconnecting electricity from the equipment. The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, laborers, contractor operated vehicles, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, to perform relocation and moving services for Cincinnati VAMC as defined in the PWS. The contractor shall not connect to or have access to the VA Network at any time. This work should also include room recertification of the medical equipment for non-hazardous pharmacy iv hoods. Testing will allow for pharmacy to continue medication for use of patients and minimize down time of the current iv space. The contractor will then return all equipment to its original location after communicating with COR, process will take 2-4 weeks after original relocation date has been chosen. 3.0 CONTRACT TYPE Firm-Fixed Price. 4.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE Due to the fluid nature of construction, there is not a set date established for the move of the facility, the current period of performance would be November 2026- May 2027. The total number of days required for the work can be established by the contractor and COR during the kick-off meeting, floor plans with the square footage will be provided by the government in the PWS to assist with planning. The government will keep the contractor informed on potential move dates weekly to ensure that proper planning can be completed. Weekend and after-hour work may be required. 5.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE From: The Cincinnati VAMC located at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 fifth floor pharmacy. To: The Cincinnati VAMC located at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 second floor (or eighth floor depending on room availability) . Back: To original location The Cincinnati VAMC located at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 fifth floor pharmacy. 6.0 TRAVEL The Government does not anticipate(s) travel under this effort. All work will be within the main Cincinnati VAMC building. 7.0 TASK STATEMENT The Contractor shall provide the following services to support the Cincinnati VAMC clinic office move operations. In addition, the Contractor shall provide all the necessary supplies, materials, equipment, and personnel to fulfil the Government s requirement. At no time during the performance of the contract shall the contractor personnel manage or oversee any federal government personnel. a. Loading and unloading equipment to move items to and from Cincinnati VAMC floors as needed. b. Delivering/hauling medical equipment, and supplies. c. Disconnection and reconnection of medical equipment, if needed, in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. d. Disconnecting and reconnecting electrical power from the workstations, if needed, in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. f. Setting up and reassembling workstations, or medical equipment, as directed by the COR in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. g. Moving and arranging medical equipment or workstations in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. h. Disassembly of medical equipment or workstations to facilitate move, if needed, in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. i. Submit Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) from the Ohio PUCO 48 hours in advance of any scheduled move or relocation, which shall be inclusive of driver proofs of identification, commercial licensure, certifications, and any VA security documentation (Privacy training certificate) if needed for access to Government facilities. Liability insurance as part of this certification shall eclipse the anticipated value of equipment being relocated and should cover damages to the facilities. j. Shall provide ALL packing materials (i.e. moving boxes, cartons, packing material etc.) and equipment to move requested medical equipment, workstations and supplies. k. Shall pack the equipment, furniture, and supplies into appropriate containers (e.g., boxes, bubble wrap, protective materials) to ensure safe transport and prevent damage. 7.1 Pre-Planning Meeting: Upon award of the contract, the Contractor shall schedule a pre-planning meeting with the COR no more than 7 calendar days after award, and no less than 2 calendar days prior to any relocation efforts. 7.1.1 The Contractor shall coordinate all moves required under this contract with the COR, facility management, and technical points of contact within Cincinnati VAMC. Pre-planning will incorporate site surveys before the move, the Contractor and COR s agreed upon planned approach to completing the move, scheduling specific move dates, and inventorying all equipment subject to move. 7.1.2 Pre-planning Meeting will also include coordination for loading docks, security passes, reserved cargo elevators and all other pre-planning required to complete the move. The contractor shall provide the COR and Facility Management with a Microsoft Word Document or PDF outlining the agreed upon planned approach no more than 48 hours after the pre-planning meeting. 7.1.3 Inventory Lists: The Contractor shall review inventory list of items for relocation, including but not limited to office furniture, workstations, and devices, fragile items, file cabinets, medical equipment, and any supplies or office equipment within the facility. 7.2 Relocating/Moving Services: The Contractor shall safely and effectively disassemble, pack, load, unload, unpack, reassemble, and set up moved equipment/supplies in accordance with the PWS. 7.2.1 Upon approval of the planned approach and inventory listing, the Contractor shall properly disassemble, pack, and load items not limited to workstations, appliances , fragile items, IT and medical equipment using the proper tools and equipment provided by the Contractor. Proper tools include, but are not limited to, hand operated tools, dollies, boxes, straps, stevedores, and power operated tools. 7.2.2 The Contractor shall use materials such as cardboard boxes, moving crates, plastic crates, bins, carts, e-bags, bubble wrap, furniture paddings, various floor and elevator paddings, pallets, straps, tape, and materials to safely pack furniture, equipment, devices, and any other items identified by the COR within the facility. 7.2.3

title: Oakengates Carnival and Parade - Organisation and Delivery
description: Oakengates Town Council is looking to appoint a qualified and experienced event management company to organise and deliver a carnival and parade in Oakengates, Telford in the Summer of 2027 (date to be agreed). Under the direction of the Council, the successful bidder will be responsible, for the following: • Event Planning and Coordination: develop a comprehensive plan for the carnival, including timelines, logistics, and contingency plans. • Entertainment and Activities: arrange for a diverse range of entertainment options, including live performances, games, and interactive activities. • Vendor Management: coordinate with food and merchandise vendors to ensure a wide variety of offerings. • Marketing and Promotion: develop and execute a marketing strategy to promote the event and attract attendees. • Health and Safety: ensure all health and safety regulations are met, including crowd control, first aid, and emergency procedures. • Income Generation - identify potential income generating opportunities to support the cost of the event. • Post-Event Evaluation: provide a detailed report on the event's success, including attendance figures, feedback and recommendations for future events. Interested companies are required to submit the following: • Company Profile: a brief overview of the company, including relevant experience and qualifications. • Proposed Plan: a detailed proposal outlining the approach to organising and delivering the carnival and parade. • Budget: a comprehensive budget breakdown, including all anticipated costs. • Insurance: evidence of public liability • References: contact information for at least two previous clients who can attest to the company's capabilities. Late submissions will not be considered and Oakengates Town Council reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids. All costs incurred in the preparation of the bid are the responsibility of the bidding company. Prospective contractors must not contact Councillors or staff to encourage or support their tender outside the prescribed process. title: Sources Sought Notice: United States Naval Academy Infoblox Trinzic Equipment
description: Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled "Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes," this announcement constitutes a Sources Sought for information and planning purposes for qualified and experienced sources to provide upgrade equipment for the United States Naval Academy (USNA) Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. BACKGROUND: The United States Naval Academy (USNA) Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is responsible for developing, managing and integrating information systems and providing information technology products, services and capabilities for approximately 7,000 midshipmen, faculty and staff across the academy�s 630-acre campus and for the approximately 300 midshipmen candidates, faculty and staff at the Naval Academy Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport R.I. The proposed acquisition is to purchase equipment required to upgrade the existing, in-place USNA Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid, which provides core network naming and addressing services across USNA. The equipment purchased will replace older, like appliances that are swiftly approaching end of life and end of support by the manufacturer. The procurement will be a direct, one-for-one replacement of the 15 existing Infoblox Grid appliances; to include 10 Infoblox Trinzic X6 906 appliances, 4 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1506 appliances, and 1 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1606 appliance, along with the associated NIOS software subscriptions, Premium Maintenance-Enterprise support, power supplies, and peripheral devices required to accomplish life cycle replacement. Delivery Schedule: The anticipated Delivery schedule for this requirement will be: 30 days after receipt of order (ARO). A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Delivery / Purchase Order under NAICS Code 423430 is anticipated. NAICS CODE: The NAICS Code for this requirement is 423430, Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers, and the Small Business Size Standard is 250 (# of employees). RFI SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties shall submit responses to this Sources Sought Notice for consideration and shall include the following information (Please reference N0018927QL222 in your response) 1. Company name, address, Point of Contact name, phone number, and email address. 2. Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and DUNS Number. 3. Statement as to whether business is actively registered in the System for Award Management 4. Size of business- Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZONE, Woman-Owned and/or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business under the applicable NAICS. 5. Indicate if your company can be a prime contractor for this effort or, if not, whether your company can be a subcontractor. If subcontractors are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and if a small or large businesses will be used. 6. If the items/services can be obtained from an existing Government contract vehicle, to include, but not limited to, GSA, NASA SEWP, SeaPort-NxG, DoW ESI. Please provide the applicable contract number if available from a Government contract vehicle. 7.Capability statement displaying the offerors ability to provide the minimum requirements to include past performance information. If past performance information is provided, please include only relevant past performance on the same/similar work within the last 5 years. Please also include in past performance information the contract numbers, dollar value, and period of performance for each contract referenced in the response to this sources sought. This announcement is NOT a contract, request for proposal, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the U.S. Government. The Navy will not assume liability for costs incurred in response to this RFI. Documentation of technical expertise and experience must be presented in sufficient detail for the U.S. Government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions are not to exceed five (5) typewritten pages in no less than 12 font. All technical questions and inquiries may be submitted within the response. The Government is determining the acquisition strategy for this potential acquisition. If any potential acquisition will be a small business set-aside, then FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, applies. Note that if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small businesses, a key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a small business set-aside is that two or more potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14. If the Government determines that a small business set-aside is appropriate and your company anticipates submitting a proposal as the prime contractor for a small business set-aside, please provide specific details and rationale as to how compliance with FAR clause 52.219-14 will be achieved, including specific details regarding teaming arrangements, and if subcontracts are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of the effort to be subcontracted and whether small or large business subcontractors will be used. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. Responses should be emailed to Ms. Sheere Reese at shere.c.reese.civ@us.navy.mil by 11:00 AM eastern standard time (EST) on 19 November 2026. Again, this is not a request for a proposal. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this Sources Sought Notice. title: Request for Information (RFI) for a Cislunar Space System (CSS)
description: (U) The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is seeking market research information to inform the potential acquisition strategy for a Cislunar Space System (CSS). The CSS will consist of up to five (5) space vehicles (SVs), each of which will require a spacecraft bus, accommodation of a Government-provided payload, SV integration & test, a Ground Segment, including mission management and telemetry, tracking, control and communications, a solution for space launch, system (space vehicle/ground segment/communications) integration, and operations and maintenance (O&M). The Government is notionally interested in procuring up to five (5) SVs to meet DAF mission needs in late CY29. These vehicles may serve as seed vehicles that will inform the acquisition strategy for a potential future proliferated cislunar constellation. The Government is looking for information on industry's ability to provide a rapid, low-risk (minimal non-recurring engineering (NRE)) solution that can accommodate the Government's technical and programmatic objectives. (U) The Government intends to award up to five (5) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) preliminary design study contracts upon Government consideration of the market information collected with this RFI and all other sources of information relevant to the effort. Failure to respond to this RFI may result in loss of the ability to participate in a subsequent program acquisition. (U) This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), and industry should not construe the RFI as a commitment by the Government. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) provision 15.101, Early Exchanges with Industry, be advised that this is only an RFI and does not obligate the Government to reimburse any cost associated with preparation and/or submission of a RFI response. This RFI does not guarantee that the Government will issue an RFP or award a contract to provide these supplies or services.

description: Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled "Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes," this announcement constitutes a Sources Sought for information and planning purposes for qualified and experienced sources to provide upgrade equipment for the United States Naval Academy (USNA) Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. BACKGROUND: The United States Naval Academy (USNA) Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is responsible for developing, managing and integrating information systems and providing information technology products, services and capabilities for approximately 7,000 midshipmen, faculty and staff across the academy�s 630-acre campus and for the approximately 300 midshipmen candidates, faculty and staff at the Naval Academy Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport R.I. The proposed acquisition is to purchase equipment required to upgrade the existing, in-place USNA Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid, which provides core network naming and addressing services across USNA. The equipment purchased will replace older, like appliances that are swiftly approaching end of life and end of support by the manufacturer. The procurement will be a direct, one-for-one replacement of the 15 existing Infoblox Grid appliances; to include 10 Infoblox Trinzic X6 906 appliances, 4 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1506 appliances, and 1 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1606 appliance, along with the associated NIOS software subscriptions, Premium Maintenance-Enterprise support, power supplies, and peripheral devices required to accomplish life cycle replacement. Delivery Schedule: The anticipated Delivery schedule for this requirement will be: 30 days after receipt of order (ARO). A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Delivery / Purchase Order under NAICS Code 423430 is anticipated. title: Request for Information (RFI) for a Cislunar Space System (CSS)
description: (U) The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is seeking market research information to inform the potential acquisition strategy for a Cislunar Space System (CSS). The CSS will consist of up to five (5) space vehicles (SVs), each of which will require a spacecraft bus, accommodation of a Government-provided payload, SV integration & test, a Ground Segment, including mission management and telemetry, tracking, control and communications, a solution for space launch, system (space vehicle/ground segment/communications) integration, and operations and maintenance (O&M). The Government is notionally interested in procuring up to five (5) SVs to meet DAF mission needs in late CY29. These vehicles may serve as seed vehicles that will inform the acquisition strategy for a potential future proliferated cislunar constellation. The Government is looking for information on industry's ability to provide a rapid, low-risk (minimal non-recurring engineering (NRE)) solution that can accommodate the Government's technical and programmatic objectives. (U) The Government intends to award up to five (5) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) preliminary design study contracts upon Government consideration of the market information collected with this RFI and all other sources of information relevant to the effort. Failure to respond to this RFI may result in loss of the ability to participate in a subsequent program acquisition. (U) This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), and industry should not construe the RFI as a commitment by the Government. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) provision 15.101, Early Exchanges with Industry, be advised that this is only an RFI and does not obligate the Government to reimburse any cost associated with preparation and/or submission of a RFI response. This RFI does not guarantee that the Government will issue an RFP or award a contract to provide these supplies or services.

Describe the company�s experience working with data at different security classification levels. 2. Describe the company�s general experience supporting Special Access Programs (SAPs) or similarly restricted environments. Describe the company�s experience delivering data discoverability, metadata, semantic modeling, data cataloging, data governance, or data/AI readiness capabilities in complex operational, test, engineering, or mission environments. 4b. Identify the framework or approach, assessment dimensions, evidence reviewed, stakeholders involved, outputs produced, and how findings informed follow-on actions or investment decisions. Do not provide restricted customer or program details. 5. Provide examples of the company�s work involving heterogeneous data sources such as telemetry, system logs, range data, modeling and simulation outputs, documents, surveys, maintenance records, or manually collected observations. 6. Describe the company�s experience working in environments where data is distributed across separate repositories, security domains, program offices, contractors, ranges, or external organizations. 7a. Describe how the company might approach bounding a minimum viable product (MVP) to produce usable results without requiring an enterprise-wide data migration, new enterprise data warehouse, or full production AI capability. Identify the recommended scope, major phases, Government dependencies, principal risks, anticipated timeline, and criteria for demonstrating a usable MVP. 7b. Based on company experience, describe whether and under what conditions this type of MVP would require a follow-on or sustainment effort. Briefly outline recommended follow-on options, anticipated duration, key dependencies, Government versus contractor responsibilities, and the transition artifacts needed to support Government sustainment. Distinguish essential sustainment activities from optional expansion activities. Identify likely licensing, hosting, infrastructure, data-governance, training, and Government-decision dependencies. Provide a ROM range, labor mix, duration, assumptions, and estimated changes in cost or schedule for additional programs or detachments. (See questions 11a and 11b.) 8. Explain how the company would represent relationships among requirements, test measures, test events, mission activities, data sources, analyses, evidence, findings, reports, and decisions. 9. Describe the company�s method for developing a Government-reviewable data dictionary, terminology set, and relationship model while accommodating program-specific terminology and data formats. 10. What NAICS code does the company recommend to describe this requirement, and why? 11a. Based on the information provided, what rough order of magnitude (ROM) does the company estimate for this effort? Example: $100K, $250K - $500K, etc. 11b. How does the ROM change as more test programs are successively added? 11c. What type of information is needed from the government to provide a better estimate? 12. List any existing contracts or authorities the company holds, including contract number, that could be used to contract these services under. title: G20 Transportation
description: This is a NOTICE OF INTENT for a sole source procurement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The United States Secret Service (USSS) intends to negotiate on a firm fixed price contract with Vasta & Associates, Inc for bus transportation services. The United States Secret Service is partnering with the Department of State, which has already engaged this transportation provider to support related event operations. Utilizing the same transportation contractor ensures operational continuity, unified coordination, standardized support procedures, and streamlined movement management among multiple operational sites. While the Secret Service will fund only its respective portion of the services, use of the same contractor supports efficient mission execution and reduces administrative and logistical complexities. Therefore, award to this contractor is determined to be the most advantageous and practical approach to meet mission requirements while ensuring continuity of operations and minimizing performance risk. PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, interested parties who believe they can meet the requirements may submit, in writing, complete information describing their ability to provide the services/supplies as detailed above. Responses may be sent via e-mail to Aisha Collins at aisha.collins@usss.dhs.gov. Information received as a result of this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Submission of information does not guarantee this requirement to become a competitive procurement. Based on this requirement, the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source under the authority of FAR 6.302-1. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement on a full and open competitive basis upon receipt of responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No formal solicitation package is available. A determination will be made by the Government to not open the requirement to full and open competition, based on response to this notice, and is solely within the discretion of the Government. All submissions shall be submitted to the Government by no later than 11/24/2026 at 1:00 PM ET. After which time, a Sole Source contract with Vasta & Associates, Inc is intended to be issued. Late submissions of interest will not be considered for this procurement but may be considered for future procurements.

title: G20 Video Monitoring System
description: This is a NOTICE OF INTENT for a sole source procurement in accordance with FAR 6.302-2. The United States Secret Service (USSS) intends to negotiate on a firm fixed price contract with Securitypro Systems, Inc. for two Video Monitoring Systems (VMS). Due to the extremely limited timeframe to secure and complete the installation of these spaces, it is imperative to utilize Securitypro Systems Inc (SPS) to fulfill this requirement. SPS possesses the requisite facility access, credentials, and security clearances necessary to perform the work without delays associated with onboarding or obtaining access authorization for a new contractor. Additionally, SPS is currently performing the intrusion detection system installation at these facilities; therefore, retaining SPS for this additional requirement would promote continuity of operations, minimize coordination and scheduling delays, and ensure alignment with existing security infrastructure and mission requirements. Given the critical deadline and operational demands, utilizing SPS is essential to ensuring timely completion and uninterrupted mission support. PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, interested parties who believe they can meet the requirements may submit, in writing, complete information describing their ability to provide the services/supplies as detailed above. Responses may be sent via e-mail to Aisha Collins at aisha.collins@usss.dhs.gov no later than 11/24/2026 at 1:00PM EST. Information received as a result of this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. The Government has determined that this requirement will not be opened to full and open competition. Accordingly, the Government has awarded a sole-source contract to Securitypro Systems, Inc. The Government�s decision to proceed with a sole-source award was made at its sole discretion and in accordance with the applicable acquisition regulations. This notice serves as notification of the Government�s intent and subsequent award of the requirement to Securitypro Systems, Inc.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source to AirEnergy, Inc. In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO FAR) FAR 12.102, the Environmental Protection Agency, Administrative Office for the RTP Inhalation Toxicology Facility intends to award a sole source purchase order to AirEnergy, Inc. for the purchase of custom air filters. Historically, there has been only one vendor who was able to provide the specialized custom filters needed for the RTP Inhalation Toxicology Facility according to the specifications based on the in-house equipment made onsite for doing the research. Based on market research conducted, AirEnergy, Inc. is the only commercial manufacturer/supplier that sells these custom air filters to fit the in-house equipment made onsite for the RTP Inhalation Toxicology Specialized Research Asset's Clean Air System which is used in in-vitro research to support New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) development and improve risk assessment. This notice of intent is not a request for quote. This is not a solicitation. Any interested party that believes it can meet the requirements described herein may identify themselves and must provide evidence of their capability to fulfill the requirement being requested by November 24, 2026, at 1:00pm ES. Responses must be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer, Jody Gosnell at gosnell.jody@epa.gov no later than the time and date identified on the notice. Telephone responses and requests will not be received. A determination made by the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any information received will be treated as market research information for future of similar requirements.

description: TITLE: Sources Sought � Design-Build (D-B) Services for the Automotive (United Auto Workers - UAW) Building E9 Roof Replacement, HVAC Replacement and Seismic Upgrades at the Clearfield Job Corps Center The US Department of Labor, Office of Job Corps Acquisition Services, has a requirement for a qualified firm to provide design/build services that include, but are not limited to, the complete design and construction for the replacement of the existing roofing system including the roof eaves, overhangs and the roof drainage systems, roof HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, flashings, roof edge pieces, etc. as needed to provide a weathertight roof system. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 10.001(b), this notice is issued for the purpose of conducting market research. Market research is being conducted to determine if there are potential small businesses with the capacity and experience to perform the required work. This Notice is not to be misconstrued as an Invitation for Bid or Request for Proposal. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The full extent of the work will be described in the solicitation, which may follow at a later date. However, a summary of the services to be performed is provided as follows: The work includes design-build (design and construction) services for the complete design and construction for the phased replacement of the existing ballasted built-up roofing system with a new EPDM roofing system including roof eaves, overhangs, roof drainage systems, roof HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, flashings, roof edge pieces, etc. as needed to provide a weathertight roof system for the Automotive (UAW) Building E9 which totals approximately 120,000 gross square feet (GSF). Also included is the design and construction of the replacement of roof mounted HVAC units and associated ductwork, replacement of roof mounted exhaust fans, and seismic upgrades to the building structure to bring it up to current seismic codes for Utah. The roof design shall meet current allowable wind loads for Clearfield, Utah. Work shall be in accordance with the National Roofing Contractors Association (NCRA) recommendations for the type of roofing system specified. The NAICS code for this project is 236220 with a size standard of $45 Million. The magnitude of construction for this project is more than $10 million. Firms interested in this requirement are requested to submit a statement of qualifications. Your statement of qualifications shall demonstrate the capacity of your firm to perform the services described above, and should include the following information: 1. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and replacement of single-ply Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) roofing systems within the last five (5) years. 2. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and replacement of roof mounted HVAC units and associated ductwork and air devices within the last five (5) years. 3. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and seismic upgrades in occupied buildings within the last five (5) years. Project examples shall include the location of the project, the project owner, and a brief description of the services performed. Your synopsis should also include the date of contract award, the original and final date of contract completion. Using the previous project examples indicate the original contract price and final contract value. The Government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; and 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements. Your submission should not exceed 10 pages. Your response to this notice, is due no later than November 24, 2026, by 2:00 PM EST, and submit it via email to Bernadette Hughes, hughes.bernadette.l@dol.gov and Martrelle Pyatt Harvin at PyattHarvin.Martrelle@dol.gov Your submission must cite the following information, at a minimum: Response to RFI 1605AE-27-N-00001; Company Name, Address, and Company Point of Contact; SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); Business Size Standard/Classification, and socio-economic status, if applicable; NAICS code certifications. Acknowledgment of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified regarding the results of the Government�s evaluation of the information received. The determination to proceed with the acquisition is within the discretion of the Government. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted and no questions in connection with this notice will be accepted. Please be reminded that a prospective Offeror interested in obtaining a contract award with the Government must be registered in the Federal Government's System for Award Management (SAM) database. Additional information regarding contractor registration can be obtained through the following website, www.SAM.gov.

title: P084 NEXT GENERATION TORPEDO INTEGRATION LAB, NAVAL STATION NEWPORT, NEWPORT RI
description: Project Title/Location: DESIGN-BID-BUILD P084 NEXT GENERATION TORPEDO INTEGRATION LAB, NAVAL STATION NEWPORT, NEWPORT RI SOLICITATION NO. N4008526R0178 This acquisition is being solicited on an unrestricted basis with full and open competition. THIS SOLICITATION INCLUDES CMMC LEVEL 1 (SELF) REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH DFARS 252.204-7025 (DEVIATION 2026-0038) AND 252.204-7021 (DEVIATION 2026-0038). This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Offerors that do not include a signed Project Labor Agreement complying with the terms of FAR 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) shall be considered nonresponsive and ineligible for award. All correspondence regarding this solicitation shall be directed via email to Demetrice Jenkins at demetrice.jenkins2.civ@us.navy.mil. Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. The facility will utilize structural steel framing with a standing-seam roof. Exteriors are planned as a combination of masonry veneer and metal panel siding. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

title: Conservation Law Enforcement Office (CLEO) - Fort Carson, Colorado, Vehicle Fleet Aftermarket Parts Upgrades
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify responsible sources capable of providing commercial vehicle aftermarket equipment and professional mechanical and electrical installation services for three (3) 2024 Ram 2500 pickup trucks supporting the U.S. Army Garrison Fort Carson Directorate of Emergency Services (DES). The anticipated requirement is a Firm-Fixed-Price contract with an anticipated performance start date between 2 January 2027 to 1 March 2027. The contractor shall furnish all required personnel, supervision, facilities, tools, equipment, materials, commercial parts, installation hardware, and other resources necessary to complete the vehicle modifications, except for Government-furnished vehicles, front winches, crossover toolboxes, and headache racks. The anticipated scope includes: (1) procurement and installation of three (3) new winch-ready front brush guard bumpers; (2) installation and electrical integration of three (3) Government-furnished 15,500-lb front winches; (3) installation and weather-sealing of three (3) Government-furnished aluminum crossover toolboxes; (4) structural mounting and electrical integration of three (3) Government-furnished headache racks, including 2,000-lb utility winches and spare-tire brackets; and (5) procurement, mounting, balancing, and safety verification of eight (8) new 265/70R17 all-terrain tires on two (2) vehicles, including environmentally responsible disposal of removed tires. The anticipated requirements, including the scope of supply, incidental installation services, performance standards, and Government-furnished equipment, are provided in the attached draft Salient Characteristics document and attached Sources Sought Notice. The attached Salient Characteristics document identifies the minimum physical, functional, mechanical, electrical, and operational characteristics required for the commercial items and associated integration hardware. Installation of truck compoonents needs to happen near Fort Carson, CO. The closing date and time for this Sources Sought is Tuesday, November 24rd, 2026, at 1200pm Mountain Time. The POC for this contract opportunity is Contract Specialist: SFC Conner Lee by email at conner.s.lee.mil@army.mil, Contracting Officer: SFC Britny Bronner by email at britny.d.bronner.mil@army.mil Please notify Contracting Specialist and Contracting Officer, by email, of responses of interest.

W9123627BA004: NASA Wallops Breakwater Project in Wallops Island, Virginia
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is NOT a solicitation. Do NOT submit proposals or questions in response to this notice. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be posted on Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ by the end of November 2026. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted for 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Norfolk District (NAO) intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) acquisition for the NASA Wallops Shoreline Breakwaters Project in Accomack County, Virginia. This procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 14, Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract. The requirement will be solicited as a 100% small business set aside. The applicable NAICS code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities), with a small business standard of $45 million. In accordance with DFARS 236.204 - Disclosure of the Magnitude of Construction Projects, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of constructing breakwaters along the beach of Wallops Island. The number of proposed breakwaters for this project will be between two to four and placed approximately 200 feet offshore (from Mean High Water elevation). Each breakwater will be constructed of Type II rip rap for armor stone and VDOT Class III stone for core stone. The weight of material for each breakwater is approximately 10,000 tons. Breakwaters are to be placed on 12-inch-thick marine mattress with geotextile fabric. Water depths for breakwater placement range between -9.5 ft and -12.0 ft NAVD88. Each breakwater will be constructed to a crest height of +7 ft NAVD88. Material for breakwaters may be transported to the project site either by land or sea. Construction of breakwaters may occur either by land or sea. Various work restrictions are expected due to active rocket launches within the vicinity of the project site, which will require all construction activities to stop and personnel to vacate the premises for hours to day(s). The construction completion date will be approximately 325 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractors will be required to submit bid bonds documents with the proposal. The successful awardee will be required to provide 100% payment and performance bonds for the project. The effort will be solicited and awarded utilizing the Sealed Bid procedures under FAR Part 14. Anticipated solicitation issuance time frame is on or about the end of November 2026. THIS PROJECT IS A 100% SMALL BUSINESS SET ASIDE PROCUREMENT INVITATION FOR SEALED BID. The Government intends to award a firm fixed price contract using INVITATION FOR BID WITH PRE-AWARD SURVEY and procedures outlined in FAR 36 and FAR 14. Pre-award survey will determine contractor responsibility in accordance with FAR 9.104. Bidders will be evaluated on both pre-award survey and conformance to the solicitation and price. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all Bids; and to award the contract to other than the lowest total price and to award to the bidder submitting the lowest bid determined by the Government to be responsible. Bid bonds will be required with bid submittals. In addition, the awardee must be found responsible in accordance with FAR 9.1. The below Pre-Award Survey Information will be requested of the apparent low offeror. This information is not required to be responsive to the Invitation for Bid. a) Current commitments and expected dates of completion. b) One (1) signed bank reference demonstrating adequate financial resources. If bidder�s firm has a line of credit � provide information on how many figures bidder can borrow against the line of credit (i.e. medium 6 figures � exact line of credit is not required). c) The bidder shall provide the latest three (3) complete fiscal year financial statements for the prime contractor, certified by an independent accounting firm, if practicable, or signed by an authorized officer of the organization. Submit evidence of availability of working/operating capital, which will be used for the performance of the resultant contract. For Joint Venture arrangements, submit the latest three complete fiscal year financial statements for each company in the Joint Venture and discuss the financial responsibilities among the companies. The Government may also utilize Dun & Bradstreet reports to evaluate the financial capacity of the bidder. Definitive Responsibility Crieteria: This requirement will use Definitive Responsibility Criteria (DRC) which are specific and objective standards established to inform the Contracting Officer. In accordance with FAR 9.104-2. These criteria will be used to assess whether the apparent low bidder can demonstrate the expertise and specialized facilities needed for adequate contract performance. The inability of a contractor otherwise eligible for award to demonstrate minimally acceptable experience as measured by the DRC may result in the Contracting Officer determining the contractor is not responsible. The Definitive Responsibility Criteria will assess the following work items: 1. The apparent low bidder shall provide one documented experience of underwaterplacing at least 5,000 square yards of geotextile fabric or marine mattresses within the last 7 years. 2. The apparent low bidder shall provide documented experience proving successfully built at least one marine stone structure of at least 15,000 tons within the last 7 years. This notice does not constitute an invitation for bid. The IFB and accompanying documents will be issued electronically and will be uploaded to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ on or about the end of November 2026. Notification of any changes to this pre-solicitation will only be made on this website. Therefore, it is the offerors responsibility to check the website regularly for any posted changes to the pre-solicitation notice, release of the solicitation, specification, drawings, and all subsequent amendments. Telephone calls or written requests for the IFB package will NOT be accepted. Prospective bidders are responsible for monitoring at https://piee.eb.mil/ to respond to the solicitation and any amendments or other information regarding this acquisition. IT IS THE SOLE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE OFFEROR TO CONTINUALLY VIEW THE WEBSITE FOR CHANGES. No hard copies will be available. Prospective bidders are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov to respond to the solicitation and any amendments or other information regarding this acquisition. Prospective bidders are required to be registered in SAM when submitting an offer and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract. NOTE: Online Representations and Certifications Applications apply to this solicitation. Inquires must be directed to ProjNet in accordance with the forthcoming Solicitation document.

description: Medium Landing Ship (LSM) Post-Delivery Execution Yard Industry Day Announcement Agency: Department of the Navy Office: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime Audience: Businesses interested in the Medium Landing Ship (LSM) Post-Delivery Execution Yard When: Wednesday, December 2, 2026 from 0900 � 1100 (CST); check-in is from 0830 � 0900 (CST) Where: New Orleans Ernest N. Morial Convention Center, 900 Convention Center Blvd., New Orleans, LA 70130 THIS IS AN INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT ISSUED BY THE PORTFOLIO ACQUISITION EXECUTIVE (PAE) MARITIME, ON BEHALF OF THE U.S. NAVY AND THE AMPHIBIOUS ASSAULT AND CONNECTORS PROGRAM OFFICE (PMS 317) FOR MARKET RESEARCH, INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY The Amphibious Assault and Connectors Program Office (PMS 317) will be hosting an Industry Day session for the Medium Landing Ship (LSM) Post-Delivery Execution Yard at the 2026 International WorkBoat Show (IWBS), which will be taking place at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center in New Orleans on December 2 and 3, 2026. IWBS participation is not required to attend this session. There will be no admission fee to participate in the session. Virtual attendance may be authorized for pre-registered attendees. NOTE: This is a special notice for planning purposes only. This notice does not constitute an Invitation for Bids, a Request for Quote, or a Request for Proposal. It should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation, award a contract, or conduct an acquisition. The Government is not requesting capability statements or briefings at this time. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement or for participation in the Industry Day will NOT be reimbursed. Purpose: The purpose of this Industry Day is to engage with industry to provide information related to upcoming acquisitions, solicitations, technical requirements, and industrial capabilities for PMS 317�s LSM Post-Delivery Execution Yard portfolio. Industry members will gain a comprehensive understanding of opportunities and be able to provide feedback. The Navy also aims to gain knowledge regarding advancements in marine technology and shipyard execution capabilities available for future LSM post-delivery acquisitions, as well as gather feedback from industry on post-delivery design integration, outfitting, and equipment trends that may impact future contract requirements. The Navy will use this event as part of the market research process. Registration: Interested parties shall register via email to Steven Maurer at steven.e.maurer.civ@us.navy.mil no later than Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at 2:00PM (EST). Please copy Kevin Burk kevin.j.burk3.civ@us.navy.mil and Stu Grosvenor stuart.c.grosvenor.civ@us.navy.mil, and provide the following information: - Company Name - Company CAGE Code and SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (UEI) - Company Website URL - Point of Contact (POC) - POC Phone Number - POC Email - Attendee(s) Name, Attendance Type (In-Person or Virtual), US Citizen (Yes/No), If not a US citizen, what Nationality? * Note: If a non-US citizen requests attendance, please include their email address as soon as possible and no later than November 20, 2026, as there is additional verification required to comply with Navy protocols. In-person attendance is limited to three (3) individuals per company. Registration will be confirmed by the contact(s) identified above and failure to register will prohibit admittance.

Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed-price purchase order covering all three (3) Contract Line-Item Numbers (CLIN 0001, CLIN 0002, and CLIN 0003) to a single responsible quoter whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and provides the lowest total aggregate evaluated price. SECTION 2 � SCHEDULE OF SUPPLIES / SERVICES (PRICING SCHEDULE) The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, vehicles, fuel, materials, de-icing agents, tools, transportation, communications, insurance, and incidental services required to provide snow removal and de-icing services across all three locations in strict accordance with the Statement of Work. Period of Performance: 1 December 2026 through 30 April 2027 (Winter Season). Note: Quoters must provide pricing for all three CLINs. Award will be made for all items combined. The firm-fixed seasonal price per CLIN shall cover all winter events during the performance period. No fuel adjustments, mobilization charges, trip fees, or emergency callout surcharges will be authorized. CLIN Description Location / Physical Limits Qty Unit Total Seasonal Fixed Price 0001 Snow Removal and De-Icing Services � Cape Elizabeth Housing 212 Two Lights Road, Cape Elizabeth, ME Scope: Designated driveway, parking areas, and old garage pad. 1 Season $____________________ 0002 Snow Removal and De-Icing Services � Doubling Point Housing 36 Doubling Point Road, Arrowsic, ME Scope: Designated access driveway. 1 Season $____________________ 0003 Snow Removal and De-Icing Services � Thomaston Housing Lawrence Avenue, Thomaston, ME Scope: Coast Guardowned section of Lawrence Ave between Fluker St & Thatcher St (~400 ft long by 20 ft wide). 1 Season $____________________ TOTAL Aggregate Fixed Price (CLINs 0001 � 0003) All Three Housing Locations Combined $____________________ SECTION 3 � STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 3.1 Scope of Work The U.S. Coast Guard requires comprehensive snow removal and de-icing services at designated Government-owned housing sites under Sector Northern New England to ensure safe, unobstructed vehicle and emergency-response access at all times. 3.2 Operating Hours & Availability The Contractor shall provide services on a twenty-four hour per day, seven days per week (24/7) basis, including Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, throughout the period of performance (1 December 2026 � 30 April 2027). 3.3 Response Times and Performance Standards Weather Monitoring: The Contractor shall proactively monitor regional meteorological forecasts and real-time storm conditions for each site. Response Triggers: The Contractor shall commence on-site snow-removal operations within two (2) hours of either condition occurring: Snow accumulation reaches three (3) inches at the respective site; or Direct notification/callout from SKC Karl Fischer directing operations due to emergency vehicle access needs, impending icing, or severe weather conditions. Extended Storm Operations: During sustained, multi-day, or overlapping snow events, the Contractor shall conduct repeat passes as necessary to keep driveways and access roadways continuously passable for passenger and emergency vehicles. Completion Standard: Final clearing operations, pushing back of road shoulders/berms, and application of de-icing materials shall be completed within three (3) hours following the official cessation of the storm event. Site Exclusions: Walkways, building front stoops, personal entry pathways, mailboxes, and public municipal sidewalks are strictly excluded from the scope of work. 3.4 Plowing and Snow Storage Requirements Equipment used shall be properly sized, fitted, and operated to prevent damage to asphalt, gravel, curbs, lawn/turf, signs, fencing, utility markers, and residential infrastructure. CLIN 0001 (Two Lights): Snow may be pushed and stored in the designated yard area toward the beach, provided it does not block egress, damage landscaping, create safety hazards, or breach local environmental and coastal zone ordinances. CLIN 0002 (Doubling Point): Snow may be deposited along the sides of the driveway and at the turnaround end without impeding utilities, emergency access, or adjacent private properties. CLIN 0003 (Thomaston): Snow shall be deposited along road shoulders without obstructing connecting residential driveways, intersections at Fluker/Thatcher Streets, or roadside drainage ditches. Berms created by municipal plows at street entrances shall be cleared by the Contractor to ensure uninterrupted access. 3.5 De-Icing and Sanding The Contractor shall furnish and apply salt, sand, or commercial de-icing compounds to eliminate slipping, sliding, and vehicle traction hazards. SKC Karl Fischer may order de-icing/sanding operations during freezing rain, black ice, or refreeze conditions regardless of snow accumulation depth. Materials shall be applied judiciously in accordance with manufacturer environmental guidelines to minimize runoff into local water bodies and sensitive drainage systems. 3.6 Pre-Season Walkthrough & Boundary Staking Within ten (10) calendar days after contract award, and prior to the first snowfall, the Contractor shall complete an on-site walkthrough with SKC Karl Fischer or designated site representative. The Contractor shall furnish, install, maintain, and subsequently remove high-visibility plow stakes/fiberglass markers along driveway edges, curbs, well heads, and utilities at no extra expense to the Government. Damaged or displaced stakes shall be replaced promptly throughout the season. 3.7 Property Damage & Spring Remediation The Contractor shall immediately notify SKC Karl Fischer of any damage caused by contractor vehicles, plows, or personnel to Government or private property (e.g., turf scalping, damaged curbs, displaced fence posts, signs). All damage shall be fully repaired by the Contractor at zero expense to the Government. title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services Idaho Falls, ID
description: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � April 30, 2030 in Idaho Falls, ID. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Idaho Falls, ID area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed-price purchase order covering all three (3) Contract Line Item Numbers (CLIN 0001, CLIN 0002, and CLIN 0003) to a single responsible quoter whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and provides the lowest total aggregate evaluated price. Quoters must bid on all three CLINs to be eligible for award; partial bids will not be evaluated. SECTION 2 � SCHEDULE OF SUPPLIES / SERVICES (PRICING SCHEDULE) The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, vehicles, fuel, materials, de-icing agents, tools, transportation, communications, insurance, and incidental services required to provide snow removal and de-icing services across all three locations in strict accordance with the Statement of Work. Period of Performance: 1 December 2026 through 30 April 2027 (Winter Season). Note: Quoters must provide pricing for all three CLINs. Award will be made for all items combined. The firm-fixed seasonal price per CLIN shall cover all winter events during the performance period. No fuel adjustments, mobilization charges, trip fees, or emergency callout surcharges will be authorized. CLIN Description Location / Physical Limits Qty Unit Total Seasonal Fixed Price 0001 Snow Removal and De-Icing Services � Cape Elizabeth Housing 212 Two Lights Road, Cape Elizabeth, ME Scope: Designated driveway, parking areas, and old garage pad. 1 Season $____________________ 0002 Snow Removal and De-Icing Services � Doubling Point Housing 36 Doubling Point Road, Arrowsic, ME Scope: Designated access driveway. 1 Season $____________________ 0003 Snow Removal and De-Icing Services � Thomaston Housing Lawrence Avenue, Thomaston, ME Scope: Coast Guard-owned section of Lawrence Ave between Fluker St & Thatcher St (~400 ft long by 20 ft wide). 1 Season $____________________ TOTAL Aggregate Fixed Price (CLINs 0001 � 0003) All Three Housing Locations Combined $____________________ SECTION 3 � STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 3.1 Scope of Work The U.S. Coast Guard requires comprehensive snow removal and de-icing services at designated Government-owned housing sites under Sector Northern New England to ensure safe, unobstructed vehicle and emergency-response access at all times. 3.2 Operating Hours & Availability The Contractor shall provide services on a twenty-four hour per day, seven days per week (24/7) basis, including Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, throughout the period of performance (1 December 2026 � 30 April 2027). 3.3 Response Times and Performance Standards Weather Monitoring: The Contractor shall proactively monitor regional meteorological forecasts and real-time storm conditions for each site. Response Triggers: The Contractor shall commence on-site snow-removal operations within two (2) hours of either condition occurring: Snow accumulation reaches three (3) inches at the respective site; or Direct notification/callout from SKC Karl Fischer directing operations due to emergency vehicle access needs, impending icing, or severe weather conditions. Extended Storm Operations: During sustained, multi-day, or overlapping snow events, the Contractor shall conduct repeat passes as necessary to keep driveways and access roadways continuously passable for passenger and emergency vehicles. Completion Standard: Final clearing operations, pushing back of road shoulders/berms, and application of de-icing materials shall be completed within three (3) hours following the official cessation of the storm event. Site Exclusions: Walkways, building front stoops, personal entry pathways, mailboxes, and public municipal sidewalks are strictly excluded from the scope of work. 3.4 Plowing and Snow Storage Requirements Equipment used shall be properly sized, fitted, and operated to prevent damage to asphalt, gravel, curbs, lawn/turf, signs, fencing, utility markers, and residential infrastructure. CLIN 0001 (Two Lights): Snow may be pushed and stored in the designated yard area toward the beach, provided it does not block egress, damage landscaping, create safety hazards, or breach local environmental and coastal zone ordinances. CLIN 0002 (Doubling Point): Snow may be deposited along the sides of the driveway and at the turnaround end without impeding utilities, emergency access, or adjacent private properties. CLIN 0003 (Thomaston): Snow shall be deposited along road shoulders without obstructing connecting residential driveways, intersections at Fluker/Thatcher Streets, or roadside drainage ditches. Berms created by municipal plows at street entrances shall be cleared by the Contractor to ensure uninterrupted access. 3.5 De-Icing and Sanding The Contractor shall furnish and apply salt, sand, or commercial de-icing compounds to eliminate slipping, sliding, and vehicle traction hazards. SKC Karl Fischer may order de-icing/sanding operations during freezing rain, black ice, or refreeze conditions regardless of snow accumulation depth. Materials shall be applied judiciously in accordance with manufacturer environmental guidelines to minimize runoff into local water bodies and sensitive drainage systems. 3.6 Pre-Season Walkthrough & Boundary Staking Within ten (10) calendar days after contract award, and prior to the first snowfall, the Contractor shall complete an on-site walkthrough with SKC Karl Fischer or designated site representative. The Contractor shall furnish, install, maintain, and subsequently remove high-visibility plow stakes/fiberglass markers along driveway edges, curbs, well heads, and utilities at no extra expense to the Government. Damaged or displaced stakes shall be replaced promptly throughout the season. 3.7 Property Damage & Spring Remediation The Contractor shall immediately notify SKC Karl Fischer of any damage caused by contractor vehicles, plows, or personnel to Government or private property (e.g., turf scalping, damaged curbs, displaced fence posts, signs). All damage shall be fully repaired by the Contractor at zero expense to the Government. Turf reseeding, loam restoration, and seasonal physical repairs must be fully completed no later than 15 May 2027, unless an extension is granted in writing by the Contracting Officer due to adverse ground conditions. 3.8 Contract Administration & Direction Contractual Authority: Only the Contracting Officer may alter the contract term
