description: Disclaimer: This pre-solicitation notice is for information only, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to solicit contractual offers or award contracts. The Government will not reimburse the cost of any submission in response to this announcement � the entire cost of any submission will be at the sole expense of the source submitting the information. If a solicitation is issued in the future, it will be announced separately on SAM.gov and all interested parties must comply with that announcement. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided as a result of this notice. Submission of a response to this notice does not constitute a request to be added to a bidders list or receive a copy of a future solicitation. Synopsis The U.S Navy must maintain and modernize to meet current and future operational requirements. The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) intends to issue the competitive solicitation N61750-27-R-1402 for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity-Multiple Award Contract (IDIQ-MAC) for the procurement of AN/SPY-6(V) Hardware, Production, and Sustainment efforts. The Government intends to utilize the IDIQ-MAC to support current and future AN/SPY-6(V) systems and subsystems, including products and/or services to design, develop, fabricate, prototype, integrate, test, maintain, and support the multiple variants of the AN/SPY-6(V). The anticipated period of performance of the base period shall be approximately five (5) years from the date of contract award with the potential of a five (5) year ordering period option. The AN/SPY-6(V) Family of Radar (FoR) systems are designed to be scalable and adaptable across multiple ship classes and mission requirements. The AN/SPY-6(V)1, which is the Navy�s next generation radar system that will address Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Air Defense (AD) capability gaps identified in the Maritime Air and Missile Defense of Joint Forces (MAMDJF) Initial Capabilities Document (ICD), will provide the capabilities defined by the AMDR Capabilities Production Document (CPD). AN/SPY-6(V)2, a rotating phased array, will be the primary radar for self-defense and situational awareness and the backup radar for ATC on NIMITZ class CVNs and large deck amphibious platforms. AN/SPY-6(V)3, a 3-face fixed phased array. EASR will be the primary air surveillance radar supporting ship self-defense, situational awareness and Air Traffic Control (ATC) for Ford Class Carriers (CVN 79+) and air defense for the Constellation Class Frigates. The AN/SPY-6(V)4 system is a variant of AMDR sized for retrofit into DDG Flight IIA ships to support modernization upgrades in Integrated Air and Missile Defense capability. Sources sought notices N00024-25-R-5510, N00024-25-R-551X, and N00024-25-R-55XX were issued related to this synopsis on SAM.gov and were most recently updated on 1 September 2026. It should be noted that merely expressing interest (to include any response generated by artificial intelligence) and/or failing to demonstrate your company�s ability to meet the requirements identified above will not be considered.

description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Title: �RFI Contractor F-16 Pilot Services� Notice ID: FA823226ACFERRY USAF/AFMC/AFLCMC/F-16-SPO/FMS Contracting Office, Hill Air Force Base, UT Description 1.1 The F-16 Support Program Office in support of the FMS countries is seeking information on how an interested contractor could provide Contractor F-16 Pilot Services � Ferry Flight Operations for Two (2) F-16 Block 52 Fighting Falcon Aircraft (Lockheed Martin Facility, Greenville, SC to Martyr BG Ali Flaih AB, Iraq) 1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it could possibly be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement; however, if you do provide information, you could possibly be sent the solicitation notification directly and this is NOT guaranteed. Background 2.1 The United States Government (USG) has an emerging requirement to execute a point-to-point ferry flight delivery of two (2) F-16 Fighting Falcon (Block 52) aircraft originating from the Lockheed Martin Facility in Greenville, South Carolina (Lockheed Martin F-16 Production and Sustainment Facility, Donaldson Field / KGYH) to Martyr BG Ali Flaih Air Base in the Republic of Iraq. 2.2 Anticipated Execution Period: March 2027. 2.3 Pre-Mission Integration & Approvals: Q1 FY2027 / January�February 2027 (flight records review, GFR approvals, ALSS inspections, APACS clearances, Lockheed Martin site access/badging, and AMC Coronet coordination). 2.4 Operational Division of Responsibility: Contractor Responsibility: Furnish two (2) fully qualified, current, and mission-capable F-16 Block 50/52 Pilot-in-Command (PIC) aviators (plus one designated alternate) to conduct the flight operations. Ensure flight crew compliance with theater entry, medical readiness, survival training standards, and badging/facility access protocols at the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility. Program Office Responsibility: All aircraft maintenance support, pre-/post-flight inspections, en-route servicing, and technical troubleshooting will be coordinated directly by the USG Program Office (e.g., AFLCMC Program Office / designated depot field service teams) in coordination with Lockheed Martin facility personnel prior to release. AMC / ACC Responsibility: All aerial refueling (AAR) support, tanker boom operations, Coronet flight movements, and military oceanic flight plans will be scheduled and coordinated through Air Mobility Command (AMC) and Air Combat Command (ACC). 2.5 Objective The primary objectives of this market research notice are to: Identify commercial sources capable of providing two (2) qualified F-16 Block 52 ferry pilots with documented currency, Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 operational familiarity, boom aerial refueling certifications, and international long-range flight experience ready for deployment from the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility to Martyr BG Ali Flaih AB in March 2027. Assess industry capacity to integrate into US Air Force operational flight packages (e.g., cell formation flying and Coronet missions supported by AMC tanker assets) and coordinate closely with Program Office maintenance and plant representatives. Evaluate compliance mechanisms under Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Instruction 8210.1 and Government Flight Representative (GFR) flight crew approval processes operating from a contractor/OEM facility. Solicit industry feedback regarding life support equipment provisioning, survival certifications, theater entry lead times, weather delay/standby structures, and mobilization horizons leading into March 2027. 2.6 Scope of Work and Technical Requirements Areas Task Area 1: Pilot Qualifications, Credentials, and Currency The contractor shall supply two (2) primary ferry pilots and one (1) designated backup/alternate pilot meeting the following mandatory thresholds: Flight Hours & Airframe Currency: Minimum 1,500 total military/tactical flight hours, with at least 500 hours as Pilot-in-Command (PIC) in the F-16. Documented PIC qualification and currency in the F-16 Block 50/52 configuration (Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 engine familiarity). Documented F-16 flight currency leading up to the March 2027 departure date (including instrument, formation, and emergency procedures). Aerial Refueling (AAR) Qualification: Current or recent qualification in military boom aerial refueling (day and night tanker receiver procedures) compatible with USAF KC-135, KC-10, or KC-46 tankers. Survival Training & Physiological Standards: Valid Water Survival / Underwater Egress Training (Dunker/HUET) certification current within standard service intervals for oceanic crossings. Valid Physiological / High-Altitude Chamber training (or altitude chamber refresher) compliant with USAF standards. Basic Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape (SERE) familiarization or tactical isolated personnel guidance appropriate for operations into the CENTCOM AOR. Licensing & Medical Certifications: Valid FAA Commercial or Airline Transport Pilot (ATP) Certificate with instrument rating, or military equivalent documentation (DD Form 759 / Flight Record). Current FAA Class I Medical Certificate (or military flight physical equivalent) valid through the planned mission window in March 2027, along with CENTCOM medical deployment readiness/waiver screening. Security Clearance, COMSEC & Facility Access: Active U.S. Secret security clearance (or higher) to handle classified flight route data, secure tactical communication suites (e.g., Have Quick, ARC-210), and Mode 4/5 IFF systems. Eligibility for security vetting and unescorted flight line badge access at the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility. Task Area 2: Operational Coordination and Mission Execution Pre-Flight at Lockheed Martin Facility and Operations with AMC/ACC: Report to the Lockheed Martin facility in Greenville, SC for mission planning, final pre-flight walkarounds, cockpit checks, and coordination with Program Office and DCMA plant personnel. Integrate into AMC Coronet movement planning, mission briefings, and cell lead/trail formation procedures scheduled for the March 2027 movement. Coordinate with Program Office maintenance personnel for aircraft acceptance, debriefings, and aircraft turnover at intermediate staging points and final delivery. Conduct pre-flight route briefings, weather checks, oceanic contingency planning, and divert emergency reviews alongside government tanker/escort crews. DCMA 8210.1 & GFR Approval: Compliance with DCMA Instruction 8210.1 (Contractor's Flight and Ground Operations). Submission of flight crew records, training certificates, and medical approvals to the cognizant Government Flight Representative (GFR) for flight crew qualification approval at least 45 days prior to the March 2027 departure. Theater Entry, International Clearances, and Repatriation: Ensure all flight crew members maintain valid U.S. Passports (minimum 6 months validity past mission window), required en-route transit visas, and Iraqi entry documentation. Coordinate country clearance submissions via the Aircraft Clearance Processing System (APACS) and contractor tracking through the Synchronized Predeployment and Opera

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services Idaho Falls, ID
description: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � April 30, 2030 in Idaho Falls, ID. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Idaho Falls, ID area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. title: Q517--Hazardous Drug Compounding Service for the Louis A Johnson VA Medical Center
description: DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS Justification and Approval (J&A) For Other Than Full and Open Competition (>SAT) Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C245-27-AP-1021 Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 05, NC05, Louis A Johnson VA Medical Center 1 Medical Center Drive Clarksburg, WV 26301 PR# 540-27-1-036-0349 Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved: The Louis A Johnson VA Medical Center Pharmacy IV room remains out of service due to ongoing flood remediation and displacement of essential compounding operations. This disruption has left our facility unable to compound hazardous medications needed for Oncology patients, placing timely access to prescribed treatments at risk. A new contract with an external provider to compound and ship these medications to the facility is essential to maintain continuity of care, prevent treatment delays, and sustain Oncology services in the interim of the compounding capabilities being restored. Due to the nature of services, there exists an unusual and compelling urgent need for this highly specialized service. The medical center requires the use of contractor due to the medical center s IV compounding room being down due to flood remediation, upgrades and recertification of the IV room and pharmacists/techs when re-opened. Existing contractual funding has been exhausted, and immediate contractual action is required to ensure continuity of these critical Oncology support services pending award of the follow-on procurement. The estimated value is $500,000.00. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency s Needs: The Clarksburg VA Medical Center requires emergency contract support to compound and ship hazardous medications for oncology patients. Flood remediation has displaced essential pharmacy operations and made the Pharmacy IV room unavailable, preventing on-site preparation. The contractor shall provide all chemotherapy agents, IV tubing, closed-system drug-transfer devices, and other necessary supplies. All hazardous chemotherapy agents shall be aseptically compounded according to patient-specific orders. The Medical Center can identify treatment needs including patient volume and treatment duration only one week in advance. Each week, the Clinical Pharmacy Practitioner will email the contractor a list of medications to be compounded and shipped to the Medical Center for patient treatment. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition: ( ) (1) Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1; (X ) (2) Unusual and Compelling Urgency per 41 USC §3304(a)(2) as implemented by RFO 6.103-2; ( ) (3) Industrial Mobilization, Engineering, Developmental or Research Capability or Expert Services per 41 USC §3304(a)(3) as implemented by RFO 6.103-3; ( ) (4) International Agreement per 41 USC §3304(a)(4) as implemented by RFO 6.103-4 ( ) (5) Authorized or Required by Statute per 41 USC §3304(a)(5) as implemented by RFO 6.103-5; ( ) (6) National Security per 41 USC §3304(a)(6) as implemented by RFO 6.103-6; ( ) (7) Public Interest per 41 USC §3304(a)(7) as implemented by RFO 6.103-7; Demonstration that the Contractor s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority): Optum Infusion Services 308 LLC (Optum), is the only one source that is reasonably available because of urgency and who has agreed to continue to provide this highly specialized (hazardous drug compounding) supplies/services for our Oncology patients to ensure there are no unacceptable delays in patient care. Optum maintains sterile compounding operations compliant with applicable regulatory standards, including USP 797 and USP 800, and is capable of providing patient-specific hazardous chemotherapy compounding consistent with the Statement of Work applicable to Louis A Johnson VA Medical Center. Hazardous oncology treatments are clinically time-sensitive, and a transition to an alternate provider would require onboarding and validation activities that may pose a risk of service interruption. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as possible (including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by RFO Part 5 and, if not, which exception under RFO Part 5 applies): In accordance with FAR 5.202(a)(2) The proposed contract action is made under the conditions described in 6.302-2 (or, for purchases conducted using simplified acquisition procedures, if unusual and compelling urgency precludes competition to the maximum extent practicable) and the Government would be seriously injured if the agency complies with the time periods specified in 5.203. The continuing loss of in-house compounding capability creates an immediate requirement for an external provider to prepare and deliver prescribed hazardous medications within clinically required treatment timelines. Failure to establish this support as soon as possible would place oncology treatments at risk of interruption or delay. Due to flood remediation and the resulting loss of in-house hazardous-drug compounding capability, the facility requires immediate external compounding and delivery support to prevent interruption of scheduled Oncology treatments. Delays associated with conducting a full and open competitive acquisition would risk interruption of patient care and adversely affect the Medical Center's ability to provide medically necessary chemotherapy treatments. The Government determined that continuation of services through Optum represents the most immediate and least disruptive means of maintaining continuity of care while acquisition actions for the follow-on requirement are completed. This limited-source approach is based on the unusual and compelling urgency of the requirement rather than a determination that no other provider is capable of performing the services. Market research will continue throughout performance to identify additional qualified sources capable of meeting future requirements. The results of this market research will be documented in the contract file and considered in the acquisition strategy for subsequent procurements. Determination by the CO that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be Fair and Reasonable: The Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE) submitted with the acquisition package represents the Government s best estimate of anticipated costs for hazardous-drug compounding and delivery services. However, the specific chemotherapy medications, dosages, preparation quantities, and treatment frequencies will vary according to individual patients prescribed treatment regimens and clinical needs. Consequently, the exact mix and volume of services cannot be predicted with certainty before contract performance. The final price-reasonableness determination will be based on the pricing established for the services to be provided, rather than an assumption that actual patient utilization will precisely match the estimated quantities. The basis for that determination, including the limitations associated with patient-specific treatment requirements, will be documented in the contract file. Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results, or a Statement of the Reasons Market Research Was Not Conducted: As described in Section 6 above, market research, in accordance with RFO Part 10, was conducted by synopsis of the proposed acquisition, advising industry of the pending acquisition and soliciting inquiries from interested parties. title: NAS WHITING FIELD AIRFIELD PAVEMENT REPAIRS
description: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) Request for Information (RFI) for Construction Project for Airfield Pavement Repairs in the State of Florida This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) Southeast is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project is for the Airfield Pavement Repairs located at Naval Air Station Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. Construction may include, but is not limited to, repairing the airfield pavement by mill, overlay, and restripe pavement sections within the north airfield at NAS Whiting Field, including Runway 05-23, Runway 14-32, Taxiway A, Taxiway B, Taxiway C, Taxiway D, Taxiway E, Taxiway F, Taxiway G, Taxiway HL, Taxiway NL, Taxiway APPC, and the adjacent Parking Areas. Approximate total concrete pavement repair area is approximately 800,000 square yards. Repairs will include barricades, saw cutting, milling, asphalt overlay, sweeping and preparing pavement surfaces. Minor repairs to concrete pavement include spall repair and joint replacement. The grade adjacent to the runway shoulder pavement edges will be re-graded, compacted and sodded for positive drainage. All airfield pavement markings will be replaced and the airfield lighting removed and replaced as required, reinstalled and adjusted to enable milling and overlay in accordance with UFC 3-260-01 Airfield and Heliport Planning and Design, UFC 3-260-02 Pavement Design for Airfields, and NAVAIR 51-50AAA-2 General Requirements for Shore based Airfield Marking and Lighting. New airfield markings (striping and numbers) will be applied in accordance with current FAA criteria and UFC 3-260-04 Airfield and Heliport Marking. located in the State of Florida. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 237310. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $25M � $100M. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 540 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.504(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. This is not an announcement of the availability of a solicitation nor is it a means of generating a plan holder�s list. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Cynthia McMonigle at cynthia.a.mcmonigle.civ@us.navy.mil, and cc: Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. no later than 3:00 PM Eastern Time on 11/24/2026.

description: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � April 30, 2030 in Idaho Falls, ID. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Idaho Falls, ID area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. title: APREO S LoVac - Field Emission � Scanning Electron Microscope Service Agreement
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, AN INVITATION FOR BIDS, OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. FURTHER, IT DOES NOT REPRESENT A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO PAY FOR COSTS INCURRED IN PREPARATION AND SUBMISSION OF DATA OR ANY OTHER COSTS INCURRED IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This is a Special Notice of the National Transportation Safety Board�s intent to award a sole source purchase order to FEI Company (FEI), under the authority of FAR 13.106-1 based on their unique technical qualifications as the only known company authorized to provide a service agreement for one (1) Apreo S LoVac Field Emission - Scanning Electron Microscope (FESEM). The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) knows of no other sources for this requirement. Notice is provided as information to the marketplace, market research, and is an invitation for any other qualified companies to express their interest in and demonstrate their capability to provide the required work. The NTSB is an independent Federal agency with the primary missions of investigating civil aviation accidents in the United States and significant accidents in the other modes of transportation -- railroad, highway, marine and pipeline -- and issuing safety recommendations aimed at preventing future accidents. The NTSB has a requirement to purchase a service agreement for one (1) Apreo S LoVac Field Emission - Scanning Electron Microscope (FESEM). A service agreement is required to provide rapid response to keep the system operational, perform preventative maintenance service, and to provide certified replacement non-consumable parts, software updates, and notifications. This proposed purchase order is for a service agreement for 12 months. The decision to award a sole source order is based on the fact that FEI is the manufacturer of the FE-SEM electron microscope and is the only known company authorized to provide the personnel to perform preventative maintenance service, and to provide certified replacement non-consumable parts, software updates, and notifications to maintain the electron microscope. Furthermore, FEI is the only known source who is capable of providing unlimited access for telephone support to the Technical Support Group, and the only known source who has the ability to provide remote diagnostics. Sources capable of fully satisfying the above requirements are invited to submit capability statements/expressions of interest providing the Government the necessary information to determine actual capability. At a minimum, this information, which must be prepared specifically in response to this notice should, must include: (1) identification of company or organization; (2) an assertion of existing, full capability to meet proposed requirements; (3) business/contracts/marketing office point(s) of contact; (4) notification of business size and /or special status; and (5) any additional information that may be useful to the successful procurement of the requirements, if solicited. These expressions of interest shall adhere to a five (5)-page submission limit plus web links and any specialized product descriptions. The statement of qualifications should include only information that clearly demonstrates the respondent's capabilities, expertise, and experience to provide the requirements described in this notice. General marketing material should not be included. The NTSB prefers that companies do not submit proprietary material. However, the Government recognizes that proprietary data may be a part of your submittal. If so, clearly mark such restricted or proprietary data and present it as an addendum to the non-restricted/non-proprietary information. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed purchase order based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by NTSB. Parties must submit information within five (5) days of publication of this notice. NTSB will not return capability statements and the supporting documentation submitted in response to this notice. Telephone responses and inquiries will not be accepted. You may email questions regarding this notice to the issuing office to Bryan J. Moy, Contracting Officer, at bryan.moy@ntsb.gov.

title: CBRND Seeking Aircraft Interior Decontamination Technology
description: The Department of War (DoW), Portfolio Management Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND), Joint Project Manager for CBRN Special Operations Forces (JPM CBRN SOF) is seeking information, design concepts, and mature technology capabilities for a Tactical Aircraft Interior Decontamination Dispersal System. The goal of this initiative is to identify or evaluate a mature, rapidly deployable, and highly reliable hardware applicator system capable of delivering fine-aerosol, dry-fog, or gaseous decontaminants uniformly throughout military aircraft interiors without damaging sensitive electronics. Key Technical Parameters & Scope: Dispersal Mechanics: Must disperse a fine aerosol/dry fog with a Volume Median Diameter (VMD) of less than 10 microns (Threshold) or a gas-phase molecular dispersion less than 0.001 microns (Objective) to maximize surface coverage without wetting, pooling, or dripping. Tactical Mobility & Footprint: Must fit securely within a Polaris MRZR cargo bed with a stowed envelope not exceeding 42" H x 18" D x 18" W (Threshold), with a target envelope under 30" H x 14" D x 16" W (Objective) to allow upright walk-through clearance in CH-47 and CV-22 cabins. System Weight: Empty chassis weight must be ? 150 lbs (Threshold) for a 4-man lift, with a target empty weight of ? 100 lbs (Objective) for a 2-man lift. Fully loaded weight with maximum consumables must not exceed 500 lbs. Power Flexibility: Operable from standard single-phase 110-120 VAC (50/60 Hz), commercial/tactical generators ? 6 kW, or vehicle auxiliary 28 VDC (Threshold), with a target capability to interface directly with utility and flight-line power IAW MIL-STD-704 (Objective). Employment Versatility: Must support two primary delivery modes: Internal cabin placement on medium/heavy aircraft (CH-47, CV-22, C-130) and external ducting/pumping into constrained cockpits (AH/MH-6 Little Bird). Material Compatibility: All wetted paths, seals, pumps, and nozzles must demonstrate broad chemical compatibility with existing and emerging USG-standard decontaminants, including aqueous hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$), modified amine/ammonia solutions, Dahlgren Decon, and JGPD. System Modularity: Complete operational system must consist of 5 or fewer major items (Threshold), with a target of a single, all-in-one consolidated chassis (Objective) containing integrated internal stowage for all cords, hoses, and nozzles. Technology Maturity: The core dispersal technology must be at a demonstrated Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 or higher in a relevant operating environment to support near-term military evaluation and procurement.

title: Kansallinen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelu
description: Kansallinen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelu Maa- ja metsätalousministeriö (”hankintayksikkö”) vastaa ilmastonmuutokseen sopeutumistyön koordinoinnista valtioneuvostotasolla. Ministeriö vastaa kansallisen ilmastonmuutokseen sopeutumissuunnitelman ja sen taustamateriaalien (ml. kansallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun) valmistelusta ilmastolain mukaisesti. Maa- ja metsätalousministeriön tarkoituksena on hankkia valtakunnallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun suunnittelu, toteutus ja raportointi. Riski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun tulosten tulisi olla käytettävissä, kun kansallisen sopeutumissuunnitelman valmistelu aloitetaan seuraavan vaalikauden alussa. Kansallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun valmistelun tavoitteena on saada parhaaseen käytettävissä olevaan tietoon perustuva käsitys Suomeen kohdistuvista ilmasto-riskeistä ja haavoittuvuuksista sekä vahvistaa yhteyttä riskien ja haavoittuvuuksien arvioinnin ja sopeutumispolitiikan suunnittelun välillä. Tarkastelun tulee tukea nykyistä vahvemmin sopeutumistoimien kohdentamista niihin riskeihin, vaikutuksiin ja haavoittuvuuksiin, joiden arvioidaan olevan merkittävimpiä suomalaiselle yhteiskunnalle. Samalla tarkastelun tulisi tunnistaa uusia tai tarkentaa tietoa aiemmin tunnistetuista riskeistä sekä kuvata mahdollisia tietopuutteita. Ilmastolaki edellyttää alueellista tarkastelua tarpeen mukaan. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu liitteessä 1 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,

title: Avoimuusilmoitus ulosmyyntiaikeesta
description: Kainuun hyvinvointialueen viralliset ilmoitukset ja kuulutukset julkaistaan hyvinvointialuelain mukaisesti hyvinvointialueen verkkosivustolla (hyvinvointialue.kainuu.fi). title: Hammastekniset työt; oikomiskojeet ja protetiikka
description: Kainuun hyvinvointialue (Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia hammasteknisistä töistä ja palveluista, jotka on tarkemmin määritelty myöhemmin tässä tarjouspyyntöasiakirjassa. Hankittaviin suun terveydenhuollon palveluihin sisältyvät osa-alueina mm. oikomiskojeet ja protetiikka. Sopimuskausi on suunniteltu alkavaksi 1.1.2027 ja päättyvän 31.12.2028. Varsinaisen sopimuskauden jälkeen tilaajalla on oikeus jatkaa sopimuskautta kahdella (2) yhden vuoden (1) mittaisella optiokaudella, jolloin optiokausien kanssa sopimuskausi on yhteensä 2+1+1 vuotta. Optiokaudella sovelletaan sopimusta entisin ehdoin, sen mukaisesti kuin ehdot ovat voimassa perussopimuskauden päättyessä. Hankintasopimuksen piiriin valitaan kaikki kelpoisuus- ja vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävät tarjoajat. Valitut toimittajat asettuvat osa-alueittain tarjoushinnan perusteella etusijajärjestykseen. Edullisimman hinnan tarjonnut palveluntuottaja sijoittuu etusijajärjestyksessä ensimmäiseksi, toiseksi edullisin toiseksi ja niin edelleen. Mikäli kaksi tai useampi tarjoaja saa saman pistemäärän, etusijajärjestys arvotaan. Kyseessä ei ole puitejärjestely, vaan usean toimittajan hankintasopimus-kokonaisuus. Etusijajärjestyksestä voidaan poiketa kokonaisuus- tai osa-aluetasolla erityisestä potilaskohtaisesta, hammaslääketieteellisesti ja objektiivisesti arvioitavasta perusteesta johtuen. Tällöin tilaaja (lähettävä hammaslääkäri) määrittää ja perustelee potilaan yksilöllisen tarpeen mukaisen, työ- ja potilaskohtaisesti sopivamman palveluntuottajan kyseisen työn tekijäksi. Tilauksissa otetaan myös huomioon potilaan itsemääräämisoikeus terveydenhuollon palveluissa eli potilaan oma tahto ja toive tämän palveluun liittyvissä tekijöissä. Terveydenhuollon palveluissa potilasta pitää hoitaa yhteisymmärryksessä potilaan kanssa, mikä voi johtaa etusijajärjestyksestä poikkeamiseen. Hankinnan sopimuksen alaisten tuotteiden ja niihin liittyvän palvelun tilaajana toimii Kainuun hyvinvointialue, joka järjestää julkiset sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollo ja pelastustoimen palvelut Kainuussa. Hyvinvointialue toimii 8 kunnan alueella Hyrynsalmella, Kajaanissa, Kuhmossa, Paltamossa, Puolangalla, Ristijärvellä, Sotkamossa ja Suomussalmella. Perusterveydenhuolto Kainuun hyvinvointialueen perusterveydenhuollolla tarkoitetaan hyvinvointialueen järjestämää väestön terveydentilan seurantaa, terveyden edistämistä ja erilaisia terveyspalveluita. Hyvinvointialueen on järjestettävä asukkailleen suun terveydenhuollon palvelut. Palveluihin kuuluvat väestön suunterveyden seuranta, terveysneuvonta- ja tarkastukset, suun sairauksien oikea-aikainen tutkimus, ehkäisy ja hoito, sekä asiakkaan hoidon tarpeen varhainen havaitseminen sekä ohjaaminen sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon muihin palveluihin. Suun terveydenhuollossa hoidetaan perusterveydenhuollon osalta mm. potilaiden purennan kuntoutuksia, hampaiston purentavirheitä ja proteettisia tarpeita. Erikoissairaanhoito Kainuun keskussairaalan suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla hoidetaan vaikeita purentavirheitä sekä kasvojen ja leukojen alueen tapaturmapotilaita sekä uniapneapotilaita. Suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla hoidetaan myös kasvojen ja suun alueen syöpäpotilaita, joilla on laajoja kudospuutoksia syöpähoitojen jäljiltä sekä asiakkaita, joilta puuttuu synnynnäisesti useita hampaita. Hoito vaatii usein oikomishoitoa, kirurgista hoitoa ja proteettista purennan kuntoutusta. Hoidossa voidaan tarvita kiinteää ja irtoprotetiikkaa ja implanttiprotetiikkaa. Suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla hoidetaan myös hampaiden kiinnityskudos- ja kovakudossairauksia, purentafysiologisia sairauksia ja limakalvosairauksia. Erikoissairaanhoidon puolella tehtävät purennan kuntoutukset, oikomishoito ja tarvittavat proteettiset ratkaisut ovat vaativampia kuin perusterveydenhuollon puolella. Palveluntuottajan hammasteknikko tulee olla mahdollista pyytää käymään Kainuun keskussairaalan suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla erikseen sovittuna ajankohtana, jotta on mahdollista suunnitella, myös potilaan läsnä ollessa, yhdessä proteettisen työn suunnittelu ja toteutus. Asiointitarve voi syntyä asiakkaan proteettiseen työhön liittyvissä tilanteissa tai liikuntarajoitteisen potilaan kohdalla. Digitaalisesti jäljennettävät työt Tilaajalla on tällä hetkellä käytössään Trios 3 shape-skanneri. Tilaaja ilmoittaa palveluntuottajalle mahdollisista muutoksista käytettävään skanneriin liittyen sopimuskauden aikana. Digitaalisesti jäljennettäviä töitä tarjoavalla palveluntuottajalla käytössä olevan digitaalisen jäljentimen ja sen ohjelmiston tulee olla yhteensopiva tilaajan skannerin ja sen hyödyntämän ohjelmiston kanssa. Tilaajan lähettämän digitaalisen materiaalin siirron tarjoajan jäljentimeen tulee tapahtua sujuvasti ja ilman mahdollista tiedoston muuntamista. title: Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration (PROMISE) Mission
description: Refurbishment, qualification, and delivery of a scientific radiation measurement instrument to support lunar surface exploration activities associated with the Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration (PROMISE) mission. Efforts include engineering analysis, environmental testing, systems integration support, mission operations support, and scientific data analysis associated with the collection and interpretation of radiation measurements on the lunar surface. Some of the efforts require the development and refinement of specialized software tools, data processing techniques, and operational methodologies to support instrument integration, data collection, and analysis throughout the mission lifecycle. The instrument Principal Investigator (PI) and team must have extensive experience in the design, development, testing, operation, and scientific analysis of spaceflight radiation instruments supporting planetary exploration missions. Team members shall work on the original design, fabrication, qualification, and operation of the instrument and have supported the collection and analysis of scientific data for an extended operational period. The current version of the instrument is based on their original design and flight hardware and software development. Additionally, the team has developed specialized software programs, operational processes, and analytical algorithms necessary to support instrument performance assessment, data processing, and scientific interpretation. The team will provide technical support for instrument refurbishment, flight qualification, integration, mission operations, and scientific investigations in support of PROMISE mission objectives.

title: Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4)
description: SUBJECT: Request for Information (RFI) for non-personal services to support the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) 1. INTRODUCTION It is the Virginia Contracting Activity�s (VaCA�s) policy to foster productive exchanges of information between the Government and vendors before issuing requests for proposals (RFPs). This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This is not a solicitation or RFP. The Government will not award any contracts based solely on this RFI, nor will the Government pay for any costs incurred in responding to this announcement. No RFP currently exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the RFP. Due to the intelligence nature of the anticipated requirements, the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4) procurement will be classified. Following the conclusion of this RFI, anticipate all future SIA 4 procurement actions will be released through the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) Acquisition Resource Center (ARC). The Government anticipates that all vendor proposals will be classified. Vendors desiring to participate in this procurement should prepare now to ensure they have the required access and ability to respond. As part of its market research, VaCA is issuing this RFI to determine if an adequate number of qualified interested vendors exists with the requisite experience and skill sets required to provide intelligence analysis and analytics supporting professional services. Given the complexity and technical nature of Defense Intelligence Enterprise (DIE) requirements, high levels of analytical intelligence expertise, tradecraft, and mission area knowledge are essential to providing the most accurate and highest quality intelligence support possible. In addition to identifying potential sources, vendor input is sought to clarify commercial industry terminology and approach. Responses to this RFI will be assessed for the purpose of market research, information and planning purposes only. As such, industry responses will not be treated as proposals. The Government further reserves the right to terminate this request and change its requirements if needed. Responding to this RFI does not guarantee participation in future Government activities. Responses to this RFI are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form binding contracts. Response to this RFI is not mandatory for participation in the SIA 4 solicitation. Vendors should be advised that all submissions become Government property. Responses to this RFI will not be returned. 2. PURPOSE This document serves as the RFI of the VaCA vendor community pursuant to RFO 15.101 �Early exchanges with industry.� VaCA is conducting preliminary planning and market research to enable design and release of an SIA 4 RFP. VaCA is issuing this RFI to open the announcement and early participation to the full market so that all high-potential sources of support can be identified across industry. The goal is to identify the portion of the market that can provide the best competition for the SIA 4 follow-on contract, including both established providers and new entrants with relevant capabilities. As this will be a classified procurement, it is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor the NRO ARC for updates and to prepare now to ensure they have the access and ability to respond through secure channels subsequent to this RFI. Responses to this RFI will be assessed to identify sources that are considered best qualified to meet future requirements. Best qualified sources are those sources which demonstrate the greatest depth and breadth of skills, experiences, and knowledge relevant to the mission, goals, and objectives of the VaCA. 3. BACKGROUND As a follow-on to the current SIA 4 contract vehicle, SIA 4 is planned to be a non-personal services contract for intelligence analytics support to the VaCA and the DIE. Services are anticipated both in CONUS and OCONUS. In some cases, OCONUS services will subject personnel to harsh and hostile conditions in environments designated by the U.S. Government as Imminent Danger and / or Hostile Fire Zones. 4. ANTICIPATED SCOPE OF WORK Once solicitated, the Government intends to award prime contracts to multiple companies, including small businesses. It is the policy of the Government to provide maximum practicable opportunities in its procurements to small and disadvantaged businesses. To support future small business requirements, all prime contract awardees MUST include as part of their team at time of proposal submission small businesses representing the four primary set-aside categories � small disadvantaged business (SDB) (including 8(a)-certified SDB), woman owned small business (WOSB), service-disabled veteran owned small business (SDVOSB), and historically under-utilized business zone (HUBZONE). Executed task orders (TOs) may have up to a one (1) year base period and up to four (4) option periods (no option period will exceed one (1) year in duration). The future SIA 4 vehicle is anticipated to include a Small Business On-Ramp and Small Business / Other than Small Business Off-Ramp provisions. To be considered for award under the anticipated multiple award IDIQ contracts, potential offerors will need to possess and maintain an active Top Secret (TS) level Facility Clearance (FCL) and be able to support work at the Top Secret // Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS//SCI) level. The anticipated multiple award IDIQ contracts will require all supporting contractor personnel to be U.S. citizens who possess and maintain an active TS clearance with SCI access and successful screening by counter-intelligence polygraph. Failure to meet these requirements by the time of the proposal submission will make the offeror ineligible for award. Offerors submitting as a prime contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) with NAICS code 541990 designated at time of proposal submission. Failure to register through SAM and designate this NAICS code by the time of proposal submission will make the offeror ineligible for award. Additionally, the Product Service Code will be R423: Support � Professional: Intelligence. 5. INFORMATION DESIRED Please address the following items in your response: A. title: Market Intelligence Notice: Fort Hood Bldg 410 General Stilwell Army Reserve Center (ARC)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of a project to repair, restore, and modernize Building 410 � the General Stilwell Army Reserve Center (ARC) � a failing two-story, 144,360 SF Command and Control / training facility, along with Non-Organizational (POV) parking and supporting utilities, located at Fort Hood, Texas. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary design services, equipment, materials, labor, construction management, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant, and modernized facility that extends the economic life of the building by 25 years and enables mission readiness for the assigned Army Reserve units. Building 410 was constructed in November 1985 and provides mission-essential functional areas in support of six Legal Detachments, a Training Brigade, Transportation Company, Civil Affairs Brigade, Human Resources Company Headquarters, a Public Affairs Detachment, and the Reserve Personnel Action Center. The mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems are beyond their serviceable life. A technical assessment has confirmed widespread facility deterioration. Key facility deficiencies include: � Roof membrane system has exceeded useful life and is past warranty; exterior doors, windows, and storefronts require replacement; interior finishes (walls, flooring, acoustical ceilings) are failing. � HVAC systems (rooftop units, air handlers, boilers, pumps, piping, radiation units, controls, and exhaust fans) are in failing condition or original to the building. � Electrical infrastructure is original, fully loaded 1600A main panel with no capacity for additional loads; insufficient outlets creating safety hazards; distribution panels and wiring require modernization. � Plumbing fixtures and sanitary piping require code upgrades; hot water heater is undersized. � Telecommunications infrastructure (Category 5/6 cabling) is unreliable and does not comply with current Army Reserve Network Enterprise Center (ARNEC), TIA-607, or UFC 3-580-01 standards; no Primary or Secondary Bonding Busbars. � No fire sprinkler system; bathrooms do not meet ADA standards; facility lacks an elevator; telecommunication spaces are undersized. � Hazardous materials (asbestos and lead-based paint) identified throughout the facility requiring abatement. SCOPE: The project repairs and restores Building 410 by addressing widespread facility deterioration and returning the structure to a fully functional, code-compliant training facility. Work includes comprehensive repairs to failing electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, along with full rehabilitation of the building envelope, including roof replacement. The facility will be brought up to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. The project will demolish and abate all failing components and hazardous materials. Asbestos, mold, lead-based paint, biohazard, or other hazardous materials will be handled, stored, and disposed of in accordance with current laws and regulations. Supporting work includes Non-Organizational Vehicle Parking and Supporting Utilities improvements. Other methods of meeting this requirement were analyzed, including building demolition and new construction; however, these were deemed unviable due to the cost of repair versus the cost of demolition and new construction. The repair of this facility is more cost effective than replacement. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $90,000,000 PRIMARY ACQUISITION STRATEGY UNDER EVALUATION: Progressive Design Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Progressive Design Build (PDB) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The PDB Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This path allows USACE to execute a construction project where the Construction Firm is brought in during the design. The Louisville District anticipates onboarding the collaborative partner at an appropriate design maturity to maximize value. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government and the OT Awardee will work collaboratively to advance the design, perform constructability reviews, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If the GMP is accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an "off-ramp" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing PDB utilizing an OT Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Aalyria Technologies, Inc.
description: NASA/Space Communications and Navigation (SCaN) - Network Integration division at NASA Marshal Space Flight Center (MSFC) has a requirement for a common network orchestration layer connecting SCaN's ground antennas, in-space satellites, control centers, and mission users across a heterogeneous set of both government-owned and commercial networks. SCaN's network portfolio has historically consisted of a limited number of government-owned and vertically integrated networks such as the Deep Space Network (DSN) and Near Space Network (NSN). This portfolio is rapidly evolving into a more complex ecosystem comprising: Near-Earth � The Communications Services Project (CSP) provides commercial space-relay services, succeeding the TDRS relay function. Cislunar � LEGS (ground / Direct-with-Earth) and LCRNS (orbital relay and navigation) extend coverage to the Moon, including the far side and south pole. Mars � The Mars Telecommunications Network (MTN) provides a dedicated relay at Mars. Each of these networks arrives with its own operations complex, ground or relay system, scheduling process, and service interface. Left unintegrated, this diversity becomes the responsibility of individual NASA missions, which must separately discover, request, schedule, and monitor services from each network they touch. A unified Enterprise Service Management Network Orchestration Platform (ENOP) capability is needed to realize the "One Network" vision for SCaN network operations. The objective of this effort is to establish a single, unified ENOP capability such that the union of multiple SCaN systems behave as a unified network supporting an extensible set of missions. description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information.
