NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of a project to repair, restore, and modernize Building 410 � the General Stilwell Army Reserve Center (ARC) � a failing two-story, 144,360 SF Command and Control / training facility, along with Non-Organizational (POV) parking and supporting utilities, located at Fort Hood, Texas. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary design services, equipment, materials, labor, construction management, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant, and modernized facility that extends the economic life of the building by 25 years and enables mission readiness for the assigned Army Reserve units. Building 410 was constructed in November 1985 and provides mission-essential functional areas in support of six Legal Detachments, a Training Brigade, Transportation Company, Civil Affairs Brigade, Human Resources Company Headquarters, a Public Affairs Detachment, and the Reserve Personnel Action Center. The mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems are beyond their serviceable life. A technical assessment has confirmed widespread facility deterioration. Key facility deficiencies include: � Roof membrane system has exceeded useful life and is past warranty; exterior doors, windows, and storefronts require replacement; interior finishes (walls, flooring, acoustical ceilings) are failing. � HVAC systems (rooftop units, air handlers, boilers, pumps, piping, radiation units, controls, and exhaust fans) are in failing condition or original to the building. � Electrical infrastructure is original, fully loaded 1600A main panel with no capacity for additional loads; insufficient outlets creating safety hazards; distribution panels and wiring require modernization. � Plumbing fixtures and sanitary piping require code upgrades; hot water heater is undersized. � Telecommunications infrastructure (Category 5/6 cabling) is unreliable and does not comply with current Army Reserve Network Enterprise Center (ARNEC), TIA-607, or UFC 3-580-01 standards; no Primary or Secondary Bonding Busbars. � No fire sprinkler system; bathrooms do not meet ADA standards; facility lacks an elevator; telecommunication spaces are undersized. � Hazardous materials (asbestos and lead-based paint) identified throughout the facility requiring abatement. SCOPE: The project repairs and restores Building 410 by addressing widespread facility deterioration and returning the structure to a fully functional, code-compliant training facility. Work includes comprehensive repairs to failing electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, along with full rehabilitation of the building envelope, including roof replacement. The facility will be brought up to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. The project will demolish and abate all failing components and hazardous materials. Asbestos, mold, lead-based paint, biohazard, or other hazardous materials will be handled, stored, and disposed of in accordance with current laws and regulations. Supporting work includes Non-Organizational Vehicle Parking and Supporting Utilities improvements. Other methods of meeting this requirement were analyzed, including building demolition and new construction; however, these were deemed unviable due to the cost of repair versus the cost of demolition and new construction. The repair of this facility is more cost effective than replacement. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $90,000,000 PRIMARY ACQUISITION STRATEGY UNDER EVALUATION: Progressive Design Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Progressive Design Build (PDB) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The PDB Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This path allows USACE to execute a construction project where the Construction Firm is brought in during the design. The Louisville District anticipates onboarding the collaborative partner at an appropriate design maturity to maximize value. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government and the OT Awardee will work collaboratively to advance the design, perform constructability reviews, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If the GMP is accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an "off-ramp" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing PDB utilizing an OT Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Responses shall be made using the link or QR code in the attachment: Company Profile: Q1. Firm Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contact (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Unique Entity ID Q7. CAGE code Q8. Socioeconomic Status (Other Than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, etc.) Q9. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Collaborative Delivery Experience: Q10. OTA Experience: Describe your firm's previous experience (if any) executing projects utilizing OTA. Q11. Collaborative Delivery Experience: Describe your experience executing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk), Progressive Design Build (PDB), Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC), Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) or other highly collaborative delivery methods. Fort Hood Building 410 Repair & Modernization: Q12. Describe your experience/expertise with large-scale repair, renovation, and modernization of military, federal, or institutional buildings�particularly multi-story administrative, training, or command-and-control facilities. Include experience with hazardous material abatement (asbestos, lead-based paint), major mechanical/electrical/plumbing systems replacement, building envelope and roof rehabilitation, ADA upgrades, fire/life safety improvements, and telecommunications infrastructure modernization to current UFC/ARNEC standards. Building 1809 was placed in service on July 24, 1961, and has exceeded its original 40-year estimated useful life. The asset is a single-story (1 floor above ground, 0 floors below ground, 20 feet in height), semi-permanent concrete structure (Construction Material Code: CONC; Structure Code: S20; Roof Code: R11; Wall Code: W25) comprising a total of 26,247 Square Feet (SF) with a design capacity of 76 persons (PN). Despite a 100% utilization rate and a Mission Critical (Readiness Tier T1) designation, the facility currently holds a Current Use Functionality Capability Code of F3, indicating a significant requirement for restoration and modernization funds to make the asset capable of meeting the function for which it is used. Furthermore, the asset holds a Facility Physical Quality Code of Q4 (Physical Quality Rating: 57), meaning the sum of all necessary restoration and modernization costs is greater than 40 percent of the Plant Replacement Value (PRV). Summary of Building 1809 Real Property & Facility Parameters: Facility Parameter Specification / Status Facility Building 1809 Location 6020 30th Engineer Road, Fort Belvoir, Fairfax County, VA 22060-5200 Date Placed in Service July 24, 1961 (Original 40-year estimated useful life exceeded) Structure & Dimensions Single-story semi-permanent concrete (CONC / S20 / R11 / W25); 20 ft height Total Gross Area & Capacity 26,247.27 SF total (16,014.61 SF Admin; 10,232.66 SF Storage) | 76 PN Readiness & Condition Codes Mission Critical (Tier T1) | Functionality: F3 | Physical Quality: Q4 (Rating: 57) Key facility deficiencies and modernization requirements include: Fire Protection & Life Safety: The building is currently classified under Facility Fire Rating Code 1 (Unsprinklered Combustible). Comprehensive fire suppression and life safety upgrades are required to meet current UFC and NFPA codes. HVAC & Mechanical Systems: While the building is serviced by water, sewer, electrical, and telephone utilities, it currently lacks air conditioning (Air Conditioning: N). Modernized HVAC and climate control systems are required to support administrative personnel and storage preservation. title: Denmark – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Udbud med forhandling vedrørende totalrådgivning til Vordingborg Kommunes fællesprojekt for Kystbeskyttelse af Præstø by
description: Vordingborg Kommune gennemfører et kommunalt fællesprojekt om kystbeskyttelse af Præstø by efter kystbeskyttelseslovens kapitel 1 a. Projektet skal bidrage til at beskytte Præstø by mod oversvømmelse fra Præstø Fjord og mod oversvømmelser, der opstår ved sammenfald af forhøjet vandstand i fjorden og afstrømning fra Tubæk Å og oplandet. Udbuddet angår en tværfaglig totalrådgivningsaftale. Rådgiverteamet skal omfatte de nødvendige kompetencer inden for navnlig kyst- og anlægsteknik, landskabsarkitektur og byrum, landinspektørfaglige ydelser samt juridisk bistand om bidragsfordeling og vedtægter. Rådgiveren skal i tæt samarbejde med Vordingborg Kommune konkretisere idéoplægget og udarbejde det beslutnings- og ansøgningsgrundlag, der er nødvendigt for den videre myndighedsbehandling. Det samlede anlægsbudget, inkl. rådgivningsydelserne, er på baggrund af det eksisterende og på nuværende tidspunkt tilgængelige materiale estimeret til 12.721.188,03 kr. eksklusive moms. Følgende optioner er desuden en del af udbuddet: 1. Fuld miljøkonsekvensrapport: Rådgiver skal udarbejde en fuld miljøkonsekvensrapport. 2. Udbudsprojekt: Rådgiver udarbejder komplet entrepriseudbud på det myndighedsgodkendte projekt. 3. Udførelsesprojekt: Rådgiver udarbejder koordineret detailprojektering og nødvendige beregninger/detaljer til udførelse af alle permanente anlægsdele. 4. Udførelse: Rådgiver forestår byggeledelse, fagtilsyn og projektopfølgning under udførelsen. 5. Aflevering: Rådgiver forestår byggeledelse, fagtilsyn og projektopfølgning ifm. aflevering, herunder 1-års eftersyn. For nærmere beskrivelse af opgaven henvises til udbudsmaterialets Bilag 4 – Afgrænsningsskema og Bilag 5 – Opgavebeskrivelse.
